name: Navy house style palette
rule: Navy is the one brand colour. Every neutral is a tint of navy: no grey anywhere. Other colours appear only where they carry a meaning (status, attention, links).

navy.use: titles, section titles, header-row fill, rules, totals, tile numbers, buttons, tab colour of working sheets

ink.use: all data and body text (never pure black)

soft.use: subtitles, hints, notes, tile captions, secondary button captions

line.use: row hairlines (only under rows that hold data), light rules

rule.use: tile borders, form-field borders, section rules on forms, second line of text on navy buttons

picker_fill.use: the one input cell on a dashboard (with a medium navy box)

tint.use: read-only boxes and tiles on forms or dialogs

reference_tab.use: tab colour of reference sheets (lists, lookups)

faded.use: whole-row font of ended or closed records

waiting.note: waiting on us; bold when on hold; italic for old, unchecked records

stopped.note: refused, ended or an error; bold while still being ended

progress_checklist.not_needed: strikethrough task text and navy italic in the date cell

needs_a_look_fill.use: fill on the exact cell that needs fixing (conditional), clears itself when fixed

fill_in_once.use: cells filled once at the top of a template, inside a thin rule-colour box

banner_fill.use: a one-line notice at the very top of a sheet (for example 'open in the desktop app to use the buttons')

count_above_zero.use: bold red on a problem count only when it is above 0

to_be_confirmed.use: navy italic for anything not yet confirmed

figures.note: Navy leads. Further series take the ramp in order. Status colours only where they mean their status. Label pale marks; never use the two lightest steps for text.

logos.default: none: add a logo only when asked
